name: The Wandering Eye

detectability.signature: Spatial metric inconsistencies; parallax errors in stellar positioning; recursive visual patterns

proximity: Distances appear to shift when observed directly
Crew experience mild vertigo and spatial confusion
contact: Interior space larger than exterior measurements allow
Straight-line travel curves back on itself
prolonged_exposure: Permanent spatial perception disorders in sensitive individuals
Ship geometry may temporarily become non-Euclidean
Risk of exiting at coordinates inconsistent with entry vector

behavior.cycle: Completes irregular orbit around empty point every 2,340 hours

phenomena: Objects appearing larger/smaller than they are
opportunities: Unique research opportunity for theoretical physicists
Hidden base location—interior space exceeds exterior
Test exotic theories about spacetime structure
known_incidents: The survey ship Cartographer spent three days mapping what appeared to be a 12-kilometer interior space despite the anomaly measuring only 3.4 kilometers externally
Mathematician Dr. Yusuf Al-Rashid emerged from the Eye claiming to have proven several theorems using geometry that only exists within
description: The Wandering Eye appears as a region where space itself seems to fold and recurse, creating visual patterns that the human brain struggles to process. Observers report seeing the same stars at multiple angles simultaneously, distances that compress or expand depending on viewing angle, and occasionally their own ships visible in the distance despite being the only vessel present. Sensors confirm the impossible: the interior volume exceeds the exterior by a factor of seventeen.

Movement within the Eye follows rules that contradict Euclidean geometry. Straight lines curve, parallel paths converge and diverge, and the shortest distance between two points is rarely a line at all. Ships navigating through must rely on instinct rather than instruments, as calculations based on normal physics produce nonsensical results. The Eye itself orbits nothing—an empty point in space that exerts no gravitational influence but somehow anchors the anomaly's irregular path.

No explanation exists for the Wandering Eye's origin or persistence. The spatial distortions should collapse or stabilize, yet they maintain a consistent level of impossibility. Some theorists propose the Eye is a glimpse into higher-dimensional space, where our three dimensions are merely a projection. Others suggest it's damage to spacetime itself, a scar that never healed. The Eye offers no answers, only more questions wrapped in geometries that shouldn't exist.

Despite its disorienting nature, the Eye has practical applications. Smugglers have discovered that the expanded interior space makes excellent hiding spots—pursuit vessels unfamiliar with the Eye's geometry become hopelessly lost. Research stations have been established within, taking advantage of the extra space to build facilities that would be impossible elsewhere. For the mathematically inclined, the Eye offers the chance to work with geometries that exist nowhere else in the universe, deriving truths that only apply within its impossible boundaries.
